text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonia has been granted an ESAF credit worth $80 million, to be finalized by the end of 1999. An SAL loan for Macedonia will be discussed by the World Bank on May 5.
- Two hundred Greek political figures and the pick of Macedonia's political establishment make Zorba the Greek concert in Skopje much more than just a cultural event.
- The Macedonian government will consider on Monday whether to provide troops for ALBA, the international force in Albania; there is concern for the safety of the troops.

- The United States will do everything to keep UNPREDEP in Macedonia, Assistant U.S. Secretary of State John Kornblum said on Saturday after talking to Macedonian state leadership. President Kiro Gligorov and Foreign Minister Ljubomir Frckoski underscored the fact that Macedonia continues to consolidate its role as a factor of stability in the Balkans.
